paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: sound doctrine is meant to be LIVED, not just learned. Paul goes down the line, older men, older women, younger men, slaves, and Titus himself, and every single group gets the same message. How you live decides how the teaching looks to the people watching (Titus 2:1-10). Paul says it plainly: live this way "so that the word of God will not be discredited" (Titus 2:5), and so that "they will adorn the teaching about God our Savior" (Titus 2:10).

Now why can anybody live like that? Grace, friend. Paul says, "For the grace of God has appeared, bringing salvation to everyone" (Titus 2:11). That same grace instructs us "to renounce ungodliness and worldly passions, and to live sensible, upright, and godly lives in the present age" (Titus 2:12). I think grace is the best teacher I ever had, and I got saved from a junk drawer by it! Jesus "gave Himself for us to redeem us from all lawlessness and to purify for Himself a people for His own possession, zealous for good deeds" (Titus 2:14).

So you don't live this way to EARN anything, baker. You live it because you've already been rescued, and because you're waiting on "the blessed hope and glorious appearance of our great God and Savior Jesus Christ" (Titus 2:13). Nobody's told me the day, so I keep my ovens ready (Matthew 24:36). Let your life make the teaching about Jesus look as good as it really is.
